newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firmer on weather, U.S. stocks.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firmer on weather, U.S. stocks.

text.p: A blast of arctic weather across northern Europe and a surprise fall in U.S. distillate stocks boosted gas oil prices on Friday, traders said.
Inland German refiners reported brisk heating oil demand as buyers sought to cover weekend and holiday requirements with freezing temperatures forecast to last into next week.
"It's been unusually busy here today," said a German refinery trader.
Spot heating oil barges for very prompt loading traded at $217.00 a tonne fob ARA, at parity to the Jan IPE futures contract, which gained $1.50 to close at $217.00 a tonne.
With demand expected to increase once activity picks up again in early January, sellers held out for premiums of about $1.50 over the screen for Jan 1-15 heating oil barges.
"Barges are moving up but we'll have to wait until people get back next week before we see things happening," said a trader.
A fall in U.S. middle distillate stocks of between 1.50 and 2.0 million barrels last week and forecasts colder than normal temperatures through Tuesday pushed IPE futures higher.
Cargo markets were extremely thin with premiums notionally unchanged.
